content.comment_body: Hello, I'm trying to upload a user program from two older [product_name] devices. I managed to successfully upload from one device ([article_no]) but not from another ([article_no]). I followed the procedure in the user manual, and the connection test in the software shows success. The outcome is: *** [product_name] -->PC [article_no].standard Upload [product_name] --->PC completed Upload [product_name] --->PC failed What could I be missing? Thanks in advance.

From what I understand, uploading from one [product_name] ([article_no]) works, but fails on another ([article_no]). Do you get any message other than "Upload [product_name] --->PC failed"? It’s possible that the [product_name] ([article_no]) program is protected or older versions require extra steps for uploading. I’m not sure, my first [product_name] was a newer model. [product_name] software doesn't connect automatically with older [product_name] devices. To proceed, first set the basic module for PC connection, then use [product_name] software to upload or download the program.

Unfortunately, that's not the case—as shown in the attached screenshot. The steps are identical to what’s described in the manual. The newer [product_name] model prompts you to stop the device if you forget, but the older one simply shows a communication error. [product_name] V8 should support older models. Possibly, an older license and virtualized XP system could help...
Yes, I followed the specified procedure from the manual, and the communication test passes. However, when I attempt to upload, I get this same failure.
The upload process is not identical for different [product_name] versions ([article_no] and [article_no]). See the provided link for the download procedure; the upload should be similar.

The key point from the link mentioned by [user_name] is to activate PC↔[product_name] communication mode on your older device. Since your screenshot shows the transfer begins, your PC setup seems correct. Note, though, that using [product_name] in virtual machines isn’t tested, and issues with simulated COM ports may also affect communication.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are encountering inconsistent results when trying to upload programs from two versions of [product_name] modules with [product_name] V8.1. Uploads work with one version but fail with another, even when procedures are correctly followed and communication tests succeed. The main challenge is the lack of clear error feedback or guidance from the software regarding compatibility or required steps for older modules. Additionally, virtualized environments and procedural differences can complicate troubleshooting and contribute to user confusion.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the ability to upload programs seamlessly from both old and newer [product_name] modules with [product_name] V8.1. They seek explicit instructions regarding any extra steps or limitations for earlier models, as well as clear feedback when uploads fail.
